messages.body_plain:
I am garchFiit as : 

r.fit[[.index]] <- garchFit(formula=~garch(1, 1), data = ts(c(0, diff(r[[.index]]$TimeSeries)), frequency=f), trace=FALSE, title=names(r[.index]))

For some series I get:

<simpleError in filter(edelta, filter = Filter, sides = 1): missing values in 'filter'>


How do I "fill-in" the missing values?

If I change the formula (and that is all I change) from garch(1,1) to garch(0,1) I get a ton of errors like:

<simpleError in .garchInitParameters(formula.mean = formula.mean, formula.var = formula.var,     delta = delta, skew = skew, shape = shape, cond.dist = cond.dist[1],     include.mean = include.mean, include.delta = include.delta,     include.skew = include.skew, include.shape = include.shape,     leverage = leverage, algorithm = algorithm[1], control = con,     trace = trace): object "alpha" not found>


It is not coming from my input. You will probably require more details about the data that I am using but because of the volume I am not sure how best to get it to you. It might be better for you to give me suggestions on diagnostics that I can try. If that gets too unweldy then I can send you the data.

Thank you.

Kevin

messages.subject: economagicImport no longer working correctly due to change in economagic.com's data format
messages.subject_clean: economagicImport no longer working correctly due to change in economagic.com's data format
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

Economagic.com has changed the format of the HTML representation of some of
their data sets. It seems they have done this to break tools like
economagicImport.

Consider the following (in R 2.7.2 with the current versions of fImport,
etc.).

zzz <- economagicImport("fedny/day-fxus2eu", save=F, freq="daily")

> tail(zzz at data)
           DATE  VALUE
2457 2008-10-03     NA
2458 2008-10-06     NA
2459 2008-10-07     NA
2460 2008-10-08     NA
2461 2008-10-09     NA
2462 2008-10-10 1.3471

If you go to the actual web site

http://www.economagic.com/em-cgi/data.exe/fedny/day-fxus2eu

and look at the source code you will see that they have inserted an entity
representation "•" for '.' in some places (and possibly more "white"
characters). 

>From my five minutes of looking at the source code for economagicImport it
seems like a well-placed 'gsub' to change all of the entities to periods
would fix things (since then the conversion to numeric would work). I
haven't had time to test that idea out, but hopefully I have given you
enough detail to understand what's going on.

Chris Green
________________________________

Christopher G. Green (cggreen AT stat.washington.edu), 
Doctoral Candidate,
Department of Statistics, Box 354322, Seattle, WA, 98195-4322, U.S.A.
http://www.stat.washington.edu/people/cggreen/

messages.subject: New release, and old problem yet again
messages.subject_clean: New release, and old problem yet again
messages.body_plain:
Gents,

Why were timeDate and timeSeries split off fBasics?

Had we not agreed to stop with this proliferation of packages?  Lastly, every
time this happen, someone promises to give me a heads-up so that I can insert
pre-releases package into Debian's NEW queue so that we would have a chance
of having them in at actual release.  

Now we again have the indeterminate wait for them and the rest of Rmetrics is
upheld as everything depends on timeDate and timeSeries.

Dirk

-- 
Three out of two people have difficulties with fractions.

messages.body_plain:
>>>> "DE" == Dirk Eddelbuettel <edd at debian.org>
>>>> on Sat, 25 Oct 2008 14:27:43 -0500

   DE> Gents,
   DE> 
   DE> Why were timeDate and timeSeries split off fBasics?
   DE> 
   DE> Had we not agreed to stop with this proliferation of packages?  Lastly, every
   DE> time this happen, someone promises to give me a heads-up so that I can insert
   DE> pre-releases package into Debian's NEW queue so that we would have a chance
   DE> of having them in at actual release.  
   DE> 
   DE> Now we again have the indeterminate wait for them and the rest of Rmetrics is
   DE> upheld as everything depends on timeDate and timeSeries.
   DE> 
   DE> Dirk

Hi Dirk,

timeDate and timeSeries are not split off fBasics. They replace the
packages fCalendar and fSeries. Their respective classes had many
internal changes that we decided to rename them and keep the old
packages on CRAN for backward compatibility purpose.

Actually we are trying to reduce the number of packages. For example
fUtilities will be considered obsolete because its functions have been
moved to timeDate, timeSeries and fBasics.
 
I am sorry that we did not get in contact with you before. 

We can continue this discussion off-list.

Best regards,
Yohan
-- 
PhD student

messages.subject_clean: New release, and old problem yet again
messages.body_plain:
Hi Yohan,

On 25 October 2008 at 22:09, Yohan Chalabi wrote:
| timeDate and timeSeries are not split off fBasics. They replace the
| packages fCalendar and fSeries. Their respective classes had many

Ah, ok. 

But -- how was that communicated? Am I not on the relevant mailing list?   
How do users know which Rmetrics components are being deprecated?  

| internal changes that we decided to rename them and keep the old
| packages on CRAN for backward compatibility purpose.
| 
| Actually we are trying to reduce the number of packages. For example
| fUtilities will be considered obsolete because its functions have been
| moved to timeDate, timeSeries and fBasics.

Cool. 

Announcements somewhere (rmetrics-core, r-packages, r-sig-finance, ... ?)

I will then retire these from Debian unstable; the old ones will of course
remain.

| I am sorry that we did not get in contact with you before. 

No problem but please do going forward.

Cheers,

Dirk
at Google for Summer of Code mentors summit

-- 
Three out of two people have difficulties with fractions.
